Write the filled-in checklist of each reporting guideline

Source: R/checklists.R
make_checklists.Rd

make_checklists() writes one Markdown table for each checklist file guidelines/<x>.yml, with the status of each item in the manuscript. An item gets numbers found only when each formatted string of each block that names it occurs in the manuscript text.

Usage

make_checklists(version = NULL, manuscript = NULL, home = NULL)

Arguments

version

The version, for example "v02". The default is the version of the last initialize_project() in this R session.

manuscript

The path of one .md or .docx file, relative to the working folder. The default NULL is each .md file in manuscript/built/<version>/ of home, without the files checklist_*.md.

home

The project folder. The default is the folder of the last initialize_project() of version in this R session, and else the working folder.

Value

The table of all checklists, invisibly. It is a data.frame with one row per item and the columns Guideline (the key id), Section, Item, Recommendation, Reported in and Status. Its cells are the text without the Markdown escapes of the files.

Details

The items come from guidelines/*.yml, after the key design of each file, as check_project() reads them. A block names its items in the argument items of block() in <version>_functions/blocks.R, which make_checklists() reads without running code.

The formatted strings of a block are its formatted value, as txt() gives it. That is the raw value of the real blocks.qs2 of the version, through the formatter of the block. So a change of a formatter needs no update_blocks(). A formatter that returns a character vector gives each element. A formatter that returns a data.frame gives each cell of each row, row by row, with each cell as as.character() gives it. An NA string is never found.

The text of a .md file is its lines. A heading is a line that starts with 1 to 6 # and a space, outside a fenced code block. The text of a .docx file is in word/document.xml, which utils::unzip() reads. Each paragraph <w:p> is one line, the contents of its <w:t> runs joined with no space. A heading is a paragraph whose style w:pStyle starts with Heading. The text before the first heading of a file is under the name of the file.

The search normalises the text and each string in 7 steps, in this order. It changes <br>, <br/> and <br /> to a space. It removes each other HTML tag, which is <, a letter, then letters and digits, and optional attributes after a space, then > or />. It decodes &lt;, &gt;, &nbsp; and &amp;. It removes the Markdown backslash before *, <, >, _, [ and ]. It changes U+00A0 and U+2009 to a space. It changes each run of white space to one space, and it trims the ends. It keeps the minus sign U+2212 and the case of each letter. So the Markdown p \< 0.001 matches the string p < 0.001.

A string is found when it occurs in the text of all files, joined line by line. The column Reported in names each heading whose section holds one of the strings of the item, joined by ; .

For each checklist, make_checklists() writes manuscript/built/<version>/checklist_<id>.md in home, and it creates that folder when it is absent. It writes no other file. The table has the columns Section, Item, Recommendation, Reported in and Status. The Recommendation is the full key text of the item. The Status is one of:

  • numbers found: a result item, and each string of each of its blocks occurs in the text. A reader still confirms that the text answers the item.

  • numbers missing: <string>: a result item, and <string> is the first string that the text does not hold. The blocks are in the order of blocks.

  • no block: a result item that no block names.

  • to fill: a prose or an author item.

The files checklist_*.md are never part of the text. A manuscript path whose name matches checklist_*.md is an error.

make_checklists() stops in each of these cases:

  • a block of block() has no string format or no literal items.

  • a block that names a result item is not in the real blocks.qs2, or that file is missing.

  • a checklist file breaks the schema of check_project().

See also

block(), txt(), check_project().
